newsitem.title: USA: Stocks power ahead on inflation data, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Stocks power ahead on inflation data, earnings.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks powered ahead Tuesday, one day after posting their best rally in three weeks as Wall Street was swept up in newly found bullishness on the latest inflation numbers and corporate earnings.

Shortly after 11 a.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 90.31 points at 6,542.21, building on Monday's 60-point jump, which was the index's best one-day gain since a 101-point surge on March 24.

The index of 30 blue-chip stocks has managed to recapture in two straight sessions all of the ground it lost last week, when worries about rising interest rates and quarterly earnings hammered the Dow down 135 points.

The market got some relief from the latest inflation numbers. The Labour Department reported that consumer prices moved up modestly in March, soothing fears that inflation was creeping into the economy.

The department said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent in the month after being up 0.3 percent in February. With the volatile food and energy sectors left out, the so-called core rate, a truer reflection of inflation, rose only 0.2 percent after being up the same amount in February.

"It doesn't live up to investors' worst fears, which is why the market is getting a nice little bounce off it," Kevin Flanagan, an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds in New York, said of the CPI report.
Stocks were rattled Friday by news that wholesale prices in March chalked up an unexpected 0.4 percent rise in the so-called core rate.
The bond market was also buoyed by Tuesday's inflation data. The Treasury's 30-year bond gained nearly a full point, and its yield tumbled to 7.09 percent from Monday's close of 7.17 percent.

The CPI report seemed to ease concern temporarily that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates again to keep inflation pressures in check. Last month the central bank bumped up short-term interest rates by one-quarter percentage point, the first hike in more than two years.
For the second consecutive day investors found some relief from upbeat corporate earnings, although the results from Intel Corp., the world's biggest semiconductor maker, were disappointing.
Intel reported strong first-quarter earnings after the market closed Monday but also warned that its second quarter would be flat or only a little better than its first.
Intel was off 3-1/4 at 130-5/8 in heavy trading of more than 9 million shares on Nasdaq.

Some analysts are betting that first-quarter earnings will show an increase of nearly 12 percent from the first quarter of 1996. But there is also a consensus that the first-quarter numbers will be as good as it gets for corporate earnings this year and that profit growth might slow during the rest of the year.
Merrill Lynch jumped 2-7/8 at 90-3/4 after reporting the highest quarterly earnings in its history. Caterpillar Inc. gained 1 to 80-3/8 on better-than expected results for the latest quarter.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 6.03 points to 1,222.44. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 8.73 points to 752.46.
